constraints.text: Replace the cover, keep the module

items.item: Corresponding L, S and R modules retain the overview's upholstery profiles, cushion divisions, stitching and feet through cover replacement, servicing and room placement.
Reconfiguration retains the complete module and service-part inventory; open connection hardware remains attached.
The Oat and Moss applications use their family-sheet colour identities and shared weave while preserving the corresponding cover geometry.

Where these components are visible or specified, the frame is 18 mm birch plywood with a clear water-based finish, the feet are solid smoked oak with hardwax oil, and connection hardware is black powder-coated steel. Hidden components need not be exposed in every image. Lighting variation is allowed; contradictory material labels or substitution of pale oak feet fail.

The overview identifies L as a left-arm chaise, S as armless and R as a right-arm seat, using front-view handedness, and supplies plan, front and side views. S retains separate cushions, rounded rectangular geometry, 40 mm corners, double stitching inset 15 mm and four square smoked-oak feet. Relevant detail views show 45 × 45 mm feet, independent cover divisions and underside interfaces; L and R have 620 mm arms integrated into their body covers. Drawing style may vary, but conflicting construction or handedness fails.

Each depicted state contains exactly one of each module, retaining four feet, two cushion inserts and three covers per module and the complete connection hardware. Rear edges align and joined upholstered edges touch without extra seam width. Ordinary occlusion is allowed; missing or duplicated modules, discarded hardware, or explicit inventory contradictions fail.

Readable dimensions associate L with a 900 × 1600 mm envelope and S and R with 900 × 900 mm envelopes. Shared callouts clearly cover all modules for 780 mm overall height, 420 mm seat height, 120 mm feet, 40 mm cushion corner radius and 15 mm stitching inset. Shared annotations are allowed; missing values or geometry visibly contradicting them fail.

Both plates dimension a joined 2700 × 1600 mm L-S-R arrangement and account for four closed latch assemblies. The before plate is labelled F01 Oat and the after plate F02 Moss, with corresponding upholstery colours. Comparing the pair shows unchanged module shapes, cushion divisions and seam locations. Camera or lighting differences are allowed; altered geometry, order or hardware count fails.

Illustrations and labels locate two retained over-centre assemblies per seam at the specified rear-edge offsets. Routine joining uses hand-operated levers; the 4 mm hex key is identified for hardware replacement. The sequence releases and separates modules, lifts cushions, unzips cushion covers, supports the module for underside body-cover removal, refits the body cover, returns the module upright, refits covered cushions and reconnects. All three independent covers are identifiable. Combined steps are acceptable if the order remains clear.

The family sheet contains swatches correctly mapped to F01 Oat #C7B9A5, F02 Moss #65705B and F03 Clay #A86E57, plus the common 70% polyester, 30% cotton weave, 360 g/m² weight and 30°C gentle wash with air drying. RELAY appears on all three target sheets; the complete cover message appears on the family and cover-service sheets. Shared fabric annotations are acceptable; missing records, incorrect associations or missing required copy fail.

A furnished view and dimensioned plan agree on F01 Oat Arrangement B: separate L beside joined S-R, a 600 mm gap, a 3300 × 1600 mm overall footprint, and two engaged plus two retained parked assemblies. The supplied living-room drawing governs the 7 m × 4 m boundary, door swing and windows; the room has 2.7 m clear height. A dimensioned, unobstructed route at least 900 mm wide connects the actual door to the seating. Furniture styling may vary; relocated openings or a narrowed route fail.

Corresponding L, S and R modules retain the overview's upholstery profiles, cushion divisions, stitching and feet through cover replacement, servicing and room placement. Reconfiguration retains the complete module and service-part inventory; open connection hardware remains attached.
The Oat and Moss applications use their family-sheet colour identities and shared weave while preserving the corresponding cover geometry.
